_comment: Citations that xref_check.py confirms dangle, which are deliberately NOT fixed by the round that found them, each with the track that owns the fix. Keyed `CODE:identifier`, never file:line — see Finding.key for why. Same idiom as state/known-record-gaps.json: keep a recurring check usable while a real backlog stays open, so that a NEW dangling citation still turns the check red on the round that introduces it. Reasons deliberately carry no per-site COUNTS: a count here would be one more number no round re-executes, the exact rot class this checker exists to catch. Remove an entry the moment its registry is populated; `xref_check.py --show-acknowledged` prints every site an entry is covering. Round 346 REMOVED X002:D-013 after restoring CLAUDE.md's rule sections from commit ee30654 — the entry's own reason ('the body predates this repo's git history') was false, which is why `xref_check.py --provenance` now exists: it asks git whether a dangling id was ever defined, so a repairable gap is never again filed as authorship. Round 348 (language C) REMOVED X001:27/28/29 by writing decisions 27-30 into SPEC.md's `## Anti-mainstream design decisions` — the registry the three entries each named as the fix, and the track that owned it. `--provenance` had already shown all three required authorship rather than transcription (never-defined in 46 revisions), which is why they survived three rounds of corpus-integrity work and needed a LANGUAGE round to close. The 14-26 gap is now recorded IN the registry as a reserved range rather than here as debt: a citation of `decision 14` would still be reported dangling, because the reserved line is deliberately not in the `N. **Bold**` form `ordinal_registry` counts.

X004:languages/whence/nuc_scripting/ncs_.reason: The path dangles because round 416 DELETED the file, which is the whole point of the two citations: round 415's next-step 1 declared it an unwired debt with three exits (wire it, test it, delete it) and round 416 took the third. Both sites are prose ABOUT a removal -- research-state.md's round-415 next-step block and round-416's own entry recording the discharge -- so rewording either to stop dangling would delete the record of what was removed. Unlike an X001/X002 entry this one is permanent by construction and has no registry to populate: a deleted path never comes back. `git log --diff-filter=D -- languages/whence/nuc_scripting/ncs_engine.py` is where the file is.

X004:languages/whence/state/harness/roun.owner: skills(B) — CLOSED HERE, no fix owed
X004:languages/whence/state/harness/roun.reason: PERMANENT BY CONSTRUCTION, the same shape as this file's ncs_engine.py entry and acknowledged for the same reason: both sites are prose ABOUT a path that stopped existing, so rewording either to stop dangling would delete the record of what happened. Round 493 committed its prediction bank under a languages/whence/ prefix because a stale `cd` persisted into its `mkdir`, then `git mv`d it to state/harness/round-493/predictions.md — which is the path the ledger's `bank` key names and which does exist. The two authoritative sites are research-state.md's round-493 entry (the clerical note recording the slip) and its next-steps block (assigning the acknowledgement to skills B). A THIRD site, state/prediction-bank-ledger.json[banks.493.note], is the same sentence in JSON and is acknowledged separately in state/known-selfdesc-drift.json, because xref_check does not scan .json and selfdesc_check does not scan .md — one mistake, two registries, neither of which can see the other's copy. Round 495 (skills B), knowledge/round-495-a-pointer-to-a-scoring-is-not-a-scoring.md. A moved-away-from path never comes back, so there is no registry to populate and nothing to wait for.

X004:knowledge/v1_roadmap_mission.txt.reason: NOT A ROUND'S TO CLOSE, and not correct-as-written either, which is why it is here rather than in state/known-absent-paths.json: that file is for prose whose naming of an absent path is right (a documented absence, or a planned artifact a next-step tells a future round to create). This is an INSTRUCTION TO EVERY ROUND — CLAUDE.md's MASTER MISSION block says to check this file 'before starting any round' — that cannot be followed, because the file has never existed in this repo's history. The block was landed verbatim by commit 7aab36a, whose own message records that it was 'not authored by a round', so both the roadmap text and the decision to point it at a file are the operator's. A round has exactly two bad options: author knowledge/v1_roadmap_mission.txt, which would be inventing the operator's roadmap and then citing it as authority, or edit the operator's block, which rounds do not do. The second site is research-state.md's round-494 entry reporting the same dangle. THE FIX IS ONE LINE FOR THE OPERATOR: either add the file or drop the sentence naming it. Round 495 (skills B) escalates; rounds 493 and 494 each reported it and neither could act. knowledge/round-495-a-pointer-to-a-scoring-is-not-a-scoring.md.
